entries.proposition: WW2 lacks significant inherent affinity for the ErbB4 PY3 motif, yet the tandem domain binds PY3 more strongly than isolated WW1 (30 vs 78 uM)
entries.snippet: despite the fact that WW2 lacks significant inherent affinity to PY3, the stabilized WWOX tandem domain binds the ErbB4 PY3 substrate with stronger affinity than an isolated WW1 domain (30 versus 78 μM
entries.anchor: Discussion, 'WW2 stabilizes the partially unfolded WW1 domain'

entries.proposition: WW2 stabilises the otherwise unstable WW1 domain
entries.snippet: Monitoring tryptophan fluorescence changes in urea denaturation experiments showed that WW1 is structured only within the context of the WW1 – WW2 tandem domain, but not in its isolated form, indicating significant stabilization of WW1 by WW2
entries.anchor: Results, 'WWOX domain WW1 is stabilized by domain WW2', Fig. 2

entries.proposition: WW2 engages a second PPxY motif directly when sequence, spacing, linker and orientation create a compatible topology
entries.snippet: the WW2 CSP pattern distinguished between native sequence PY1PY2, reminiscent of PY3, and PY1PY2S (poly G linker), PY1PY3, and PY3PY3 for which large WW2 CSPs suggest a strong interaction with this domain as well

entries.proposition: The strongest direct WW2 engagement requires a short engineered linker; the native ErbB4 PY1PY2 linker gives a weaker interaction
entries.snippet: To some extent, this is due to the longer native linker connecting PY1 and PY2, since the interaction grew stronger when a shorter flexible non-native polyglycine linker (similar to the one in the other two double-motif peptides) was used
